claims.text: Houston Methodist is deploying Aidoc, an AI-powered imaging platform.
claims.quote: Houston Methodist is deploying Aidoc, an AI-powered imaging platform that enhances radiology workflows, accelerates emergency response and strengthens patient follow-up, helping improve outcomes and streamline care across the system.

claims.text: Aidoc automatically flags potential issues and displays a visual heat map to help guide radiologists' attention.
claims.quote: The specific tool, called Aidoc, automatically flags potential issues and displays a visual heat map to help guide radiologists’ attention.

claims.text: When a significant concern is identified, exams can be prioritized to the top of the radiologist's worklist for faster review.
claims.quote: When a significant concern is identified, exams can be prioritized to the top of the radiologist’s worklist, enabling faster review.

claims.text: The radiology phase began with 18 super users testing the platform, with expansion to roughly 100 radiologists on June 22nd.
claims.quote: The first phase of the rollout focuses on radiology, with 18 “super users” beginning testing of the platform and expansion to roughly 100 radiologists in June 22.

claims.text: Ginny Torno, Sr. Director of Information Technology and Innovation, is leading the implementation.
claims.quote: said Ginny Torno, Sr. Director of Information Technology and Innovation, who is leading the implementation.

claims.text: Torno said the system showed very positive returns after just a couple of days.
claims.quote: “We’re already seeing very positive returns after just a couple of days,” said Ginny Torno

claims.text: Radiologists were initially skeptical, and even the most skeptical one called it a great tool.
claims.quote: Initially skeptical, radiologists are quickly adopting the tool and learning how it can help them. “Even the most skeptical radiologist said, ‘This is a great tool. We can’t wait until they have more algorithms to check."

claims.text: An image routing system automatically delivers the appropriate studies for analysis without extra steps from radiologists, and technologists do nothing to make it route correctly.
claims.quote: Houston Methodist implemented an advanced image routing system that automatically delivers the appropriate studies for analysis — without requiring extra steps from radiologists. “Technologists don’t do anything to make it route correctly. All of the logic is built in the router and can be easily managed over time as we add and change imaging procedures.”

claims.text: Enterprise-wide intelligent image routing was previously not possible without manually configuring each scanner.
claims.quote: enabling intelligent image routing across the enterprise — something previously not possible without manually configuring each scanner.

claims.text: The second phase introduces mobile tools for stroke and pulmonary embolism care teams that alert physicians and nurses in real time when imaging suggests a potential emergency.
claims.quote: The second phase of the initiative introduces mobile tools for stroke and pulmonary embolism (PE) care teams. These applications will alert physicians and nurses in real time when imaging suggests a potential emergency.

claims.text: Clinicians can view images on mobile devices, optimized for triage rather than diagnosis, and activate response teams immediately.
claims.quote: Clinicians can quickly view images on their mobile devices (optimized for triage rather than diagnosis) and activate response teams immediately.

claims.text: Houston Methodist already has a stroke app it will replace but had nothing for PE.
claims.quote: “We do have a stroke app already that we’re going to replace, but we don’t have anything for PE,” Torno said.

claims.text: A patient management tool was announced for later in 2026 to scan health record data for follow-up needs such as referrals in physician notes, primarily supporting nurse coordinators.
claims.quote: Later this year, Houston Methodist will introduce a patient management tool that scans electronic health record data to help identify potential follow-up needs — such as referrals documented in physician notes — and ensure they are not missed. This capability will primarily support nurse coordinators

claims.text: The technology is already in use at more than 100 hospitals nationwide.
claims.quote: The technology is already in use at more than 100 hospitals nationwide.

claims.text: Torno said the system is not perfect, the vendor is upfront about that, and it makes a change every time it gets feedback.
claims.quote: “It’s not perfect, but they’re upfront about that,” she noted. “Every time they get feedback, they make a change.”

claims.text: New FDA-approved algorithms are expected to expand the system's reach.
claims.quote: Additional capabilities are expected soon, with new FDA-approved algorithms expanding the system’s reach as part of the organization’s broader licensing agreement.

claims.text: Pulmonary embolism occurs when a blood clot breaks loose and travels through the bloodstream to the lungs.
claims.quote: Pulmonary embolism is a type of venous thromboembolism (VTE) that occurs when a blood clot breaks loose and travels through the bloodstream to the lungs.

claims.text: CT pulmonary angiography is the main test to diagnose pulmonary embolism.
claims.quote: Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) takes pictures of your blood vessels and looks for blood clots in the lungs. It is the main test to diagnose pulmonary embolism.

claims.text: Pulmonary embolism may lead to life-threatening complications and death.
claims.quote: Pulmonary embolism should be taken seriously, as it may lead to life-threatening complications and death.

claims.text: Aidoc was established in 2016 and first focused on flagging acute anomalies in real time for radiologists.
claims.quote: Established in 2016, Aidoc’s solutions first focused on aiding radiologists in reducing turnaround time and increasing quality and efficiency by flagging acute anomalies in real time.

claims.text: A 2006 Stroke journal study estimated that a typical patient loses 1.9 million neurons each minute a stroke goes untreated.
claims.quote: The typical patient loses 1.9 million neurons each minute in which stroke is untreated.

claims.text: Houston Methodist Hospital, the system's flagship, is in the Texas Medical Center.
claims.quote: Houston Methodist Hospital, our flagship in the Texas Medical Center and seven hospitals located throughout Greater Houston
